Multi-Station Cold Heading ↗

Wire is cut and formed through a sequence of dies. Head, flange and some shoulder features can be integrated into a repeatable production route.

ROUTE 02 / BAR MACHINING

Swiss-Type & CNC Turning ↗

Bar-fed turning and turn-mill operations create drawing-specific steps, bores and other details with flexible programming.

Hot Heading & Forging ↗

Heated stock can be formed into larger or heavier geometries before finishing operations define the final interfaces.

PROCESS / THREAD GENERATION

Thread Rolling, Cutting & Tapping ↗

The thread profile, material and batch conditions determine whether rolling, cutting, grinding or an internal tapping process is appropriate.

PROCESS / FUNCTIONAL FEATURES

Secondary & Precision Operations ↗

Local holes, flats, grooves and finished diameters often create the functional difference in a non-standard fastener.

PROCESS / MATERIAL CONDITION

Material-Specific Heat Treatment ↗

Heat-treatment selection follows the alloy, required condition and applicable acceptance specification. One sequence cannot be applied to every screw.

PROCESS / SURFACE SYSTEM

Coatings & Surface Treatments ↗

Specify a complete surface system: substrate condition, coating, thickness, functional surfaces and acceptance criteria.

PROCESS / FINAL CONDITION

Cleaning, Locking & Assembly ↗

Cleanliness, burr control and pre-applied features are part of the finished-part specification, not an afterthought.

PROCESS / ACCEPTANCE

CCD Vision & Dimensional Inspection ↗

Non-contact optical checks for screw length, head diameter and visible stepped profiles, combined with the gauges and tests required by the drawing.

Full inspection where it is justified.

Agree which features need 100% screening and which use an approved sampling plan. Full dimensional screening does not replace material or destructive test requirements.

CCD optical dimensional inspection, thread gauges and mechanical testing address different characteristics. Availability and any external laboratory arrangements are confirmed in the quotation.

Shoulder fits, thread classes and when grinding matters

A shaft fit and a thread tolerance class control different interfaces. Write the required function clearly before deciding how the surfaces must be finished.

ZUFEK Technical Resources • Published October 29, 2026
IN THIS GUIDESeparate the plain shoulder and the threadIdentify the mating relationshipSpecify grinding only with a reasonInspect after the relevant finishing stage
RELATED PRODUCTShoulder Screws ↗

Separate the plain shoulder and the thread

A shaft tolerance such as g6 or h7 describes a plain cylindrical feature. A designation such as 6g or 6H belongs to a metric thread tolerance system. Case and order matter; these are not interchangeable callouts.

Identify the mating relationship

Provide the mating bore, shoulder length, datums and surface texture. Clearance, locating behavior and rotation depend on both components and their operating conditions.

Working on this type of part? Explore our shoulder screws and include the functional requirements in your RFQ.

Specify grinding only with a reason

Grinding can be useful for size, form and surface finish, especially after a treatment that changes dimensions. A tolerance designation alone does not prove that centerless grinding is the only acceptable route.

Inspect after the relevant finishing stage

Review coating allowance and final condition. Agree measurement methods for size, form and datum relationships, together with thread gauging and the required inspection records.

Thread Rolling, Cutting & Tapping

The thread profile, material and batch conditions determine whether rolling, cutting, grinding or an internal tapping process is appropriate.

Flat-die and cylindrical-die rolling

External threads are formed by displacement. Suitable material condition, blank diameter and tool geometry are essential. Machine capability sets the actual size range; no universal M0.8–M12 limit applies.

Single-point cutting and special profiles

Turning can address specified pitches, tapers and special profiles where tooling and access permit. NPT, MJ and other named threads require the applicable complete specification, not an approximate profile.

Internal cut and form tapping

Cut tapping removes material; form tapping displaces a sufficiently ductile material and needs the correct pre-hole. Neither method is universally stronger in every grade and geometry.

Acceptance and sequence

Define designation, class, usable length, runout and gauging. Rolling may improve fatigue behavior in suitable conditions, but is not a blanket strength guarantee. Review whether threading occurs before or after heat treatment.

PROCESS / MATERIAL CONDITION

Material-Specific Heat Treatment

Heat-treatment selection follows the alloy, required condition and applicable acceptance specification. One sequence cannot be applied to every screw.

MANUFACTURING CAPABILITIESMulti-Station Cold HeadingSwiss-Type & CNC TurningHot Heading & ForgingCold Heading + Secondary MachiningThread Rolling, Cutting & TappingSecondary & Precision OperationsMaterial-Specific Heat TreatmentCoatings & Surface TreatmentsCleaning, Locking & AssemblyCCD Vision & Dimensional InspectionComplete route examples ↗

Quench and temper

Suitable carbon and alloy steels can be processed to specified mechanical requirements. Property classes such as 8.8, 10.9 and 12.9 require an applicable specification and verification; treatment names alone do not establish the class.

Case hardening and boron steel

Carburizing and hardening can produce a hardened surface with a different core condition. A grade such as 10B21 does not by itself prescribe carburizing: specify core properties, case requirements and application.

Stainless and titanium distinctions

304/316 austenitic stainless steels are not precipitation-hardening grades. Solution annealing serves a different purpose from aging 17-4PH. Titanium and other alloys need grade-specific treatment; do not transfer a stainless cycle to them.

Stress relief and stability

Stress-relief or specialist cryogenic treatments are selected only where justified by material condition and dimensional needs. State the required final condition and review distortion, corrosion and finish compatibility.

Coatings & Surface Treatments

Specify a complete surface system: substrate condition, coating, thickness, functional surfaces and acceptance criteria.

Electroplated finishes

Zinc, colored or black zinc systems, bright/black nickel and zinc-nickel are discussion options. Name the actual coating specification, thickness and any friction or corrosion-test requirement. Cadmium is a restricted specialist option requiring project-specific review, not a default finish.

Zinc-flake and conversion systems

Zinc-flake systems, including Dacromet- or Geomet-type requirements, need an exact specification and applicability review. Black oxide and passivation depend on the substrate. Non-electrolytic deposition does not remove every possible hydrogen source from the full process.

Organic and vacuum coatings

Electrophoretic coating, PTFE-based coatings, powder/paint and PVD can address selected friction, appearance or surface functions. Thickness, cure temperature and thread fit need review.

High-strength fastener review

High-strength or high-hardness steels may be susceptible to hydrogen embrittlement from cleaning, pickling or plating. Baking and process controls can reduce risk but cannot guarantee its elimination. Select the coating and relief requirements under the applicable specification; neither a blanket zinc ban nor a blanket bake rule is sufficient.

Cleaning and burr control

PROCESS / ACCEPTANCE

CCD Vision & Dimensional Inspection

Non-contact optical checks for screw length, head diameter and visible stepped profiles, combined with the gauges and tests required by the drawing.

CCD optical dimension checks

Camera-based vision measurement uses suitable optics, lighting and calibrated edge detection to check accessible external dimensions such as overall length, head diameter and shoulder profile. A stable presentation and validated inspection program are needed for the specified part.

Complementary verification

Silhouette inspection does not establish internal geometry, material strength or every thread characteristic. Use the specified thread gauges, additional dimensional methods and functional tests where required. Agree acceptance criteria and the actual inspection coverage.

Material and mechanical checks

Material documentation, HV/HRC hardness, tensile, torque or destructive testing are selected when applicable. A test name needs a method, sample quantity and acceptance criterion.

Surface and specialist checks

Coating thickness, specified salt-spray testing, metallography, fatigue and hydrogen-embrittlement evaluation require an agreed scope. Salt spray results do not directly predict service life.

Sampling versus full inspection

Agree which characteristics receive 100% screening, sampling or first-article approval. Equipment availability, external laboratory work and reporting are confirmed for the order; no unverified in-house laboratory claim is made.
